answer: An attacker who floods the jury with fake votes also floods itself with the cost of its own dishonest votes, because every vote is penalized when it backs a bad answer. In practice this means a farm must spend real resources on every single alias, and that per-identity cost is what keeps the network honest at scale.. It is effective because voting power is weighted by verifiable work over time, so a fresh flood of accounts cannot manufacture a decisive vote. Consider a umber as the anchor of the cost.
